MDmanager-conversations.mdTrao đổi 1:1, risk, quyết định, quản lý · 37 lines⌄

Manager conversations

Cập nhật ngắn, chủ động, không phóng đại tiến độ và cho thấy mình đang kết nối các team.

Reusable phrases

Situation Natural sentence Simpler alternative More professional alternative
Update Quick update from my side: the review is on track. The review is going well. A brief update from my side: the review is on track, with one open dependency.
Blocker We need input from the network team. The network team needs to help. The remaining blocker is the network decision; I have asked the owner to confirm by tomorrow.
Ask priority Which item should I review first? What is the top priority? Could you confirm which item has the highest business priority this week?
Own follow-up I will coordinate the next step. I will follow up. I will coordinate the technical follow-up and share a clear recommendation.

Realistic dialogue

Weekly one-to-one

Manager: What did you focus on this week?
You: I reviewed the GCP migration and helped two teams with production issues.
Manager: What is the main risk?
You: The migration test does not cover duplicate processing yet. I asked the team to add that case.
Manager: Do you need support?
You: Please help confirm the business owner for the acceptance criteria. I will handle the technical review.

When the answer is not ready

Manager: Can we approve the design today?
You: I am not ready to recommend approval yet.
Manager: What is missing?
You: We need one load test and a rollback check. I can give you a clear answer by Friday morning.

Useful vocabulary and collocations

  • quick update — cập nhật nhanh
  • open dependency — dependency chưa được giải quyết
  • business priority — ưu tiên nghiệp vụ
  • coordinate the follow-up — điều phối bước tiếp theo
MDmeetings.mdMở họp, refocus, quyết định, chốt action · 37 lines⌄

Meetings

Dùng để mở cuộc họp, giữ đúng phạm vi, làm rõ quyết định và chốt action.

Reusable phrases

Situation Natural sentence Simpler alternative More professional alternative
Open Let us start with the main decision. What do we need to decide? I suggest we begin with the decision we need today.
Clarify Let me check that I understood you. Do you mean this? Let me confirm my understanding before we continue.
Refocus Can we come back to the main point? Back to the main point. Could we return to the main question and park the detail for later?
Close Let us confirm the owner and due date. Who will do it, and when? Before we close, could we confirm the action, owner, and target date?

Realistic dialogue

A decision meeting

PMO: We have twenty minutes. Can we agree on an option today?
You: Yes. I see two workable options. The first is safer for this release.
Architect: Why do you prefer it?
You: It changes less and gives us a clear rollback. The cost is one extra week.
PMO: Can the team accept that?
You: Let us confirm with the team now, then record the decision and owner.

When people speak fast

Manager: We should align the rollout with the platform window and the regional freeze.
You: I caught the rollout part, but not the date. Could you repeat the date slowly?
Manager: Thursday the twenty-sixth.
You: Thanks. I will put Thursday the twenty-sixth in the chat so we all have the same date.

Useful vocabulary and collocations

  • decision required — quyết định cần đưa ra
  • park this topic — tạm để chủ đề sang phần sau
  • action owner — người chịu trách nhiệm action
  • target date — ngày dự kiến hoàn thành
MDpresentations.mdSteering update, slide signposting, demo · 29 lines⌄

Presentations

Cấu trúc phần trình bày ngắn cho architecture review, steering meeting và demo.

Reusable phrases

Situation Natural sentence Simpler alternative More professional alternative
Start Today I will cover three points. I have three points. Today I will cover the current issue, the options, and my recommendation.
Signpost The key point on this slide is the risk. This slide shows the risk. The main point to take from this slide is the operational risk.
Handle question That is a good question. Let me answer it in two parts. Let me answer in two parts. Thank you. I would separate the technical answer from the delivery impact.
End My recommendation is to start small and measure. Let us start small. My recommendation is a controlled pilot with clear success and rollback criteria.

Realistic dialogue

Steering update

You: Today I will cover the issue, the options, and my recommendation.
Leader: Can you start with the business impact?
You: Of course. Five projects are affected, but production is still stable.
Leader: What do you need from us?
You: We need a decision on the pilot scope and one business owner for acceptance.

Useful vocabulary and collocations

  • key takeaway — ý chính cần nhớ
  • business impact — ảnh hưởng nghiệp vụ
  • controlled pilot — pilot có giới hạn và kiểm soát
  • success criteria — tiêu chí thành công
MDtechnical-advisor.mdGiới thiệu role TA và cross-project alignment · 49 lines⌄

Technical Advisor - English

Mẫu câu giúp người khác thấy rõ bạn tư vấn, đánh giá, kết nối và hỗ trợ quyết định xuyên dự án.

Reusable phrases

Situation Natural sentence Simpler alternative More professional alternative
Describe role I help teams make sound technical decisions. I help teams choose good solutions. I advise teams on architecture, delivery risk, and production readiness across projects.
AI use I use AI to explore options and speed up analysis. AI helps me review and check ideas. I use AI as a technical thought partner, then validate the output with project context and evidence.
Review My role is to ask the questions that reduce risk. I help find risks early. I provide an independent technical view and help teams address risks before production.
Support I do not take over the team’s work; I help them move forward. I guide the team. I support the team with options, trade-offs, and a clear path to a decision.

Realistic dialogue

Explaining the TA role

PMO: Are you the technical lead for this project?
You: The project has its own technical lead. I support several projects as a Technical Advisor.
PMO: What does that include?
You: I review important designs, highlight cross-project risks, and help teams prepare for production.
PMO: Who makes the final decision?
You: The accountable project owner makes it. I provide the technical recommendation and evidence.

AI coding survey

Manager: How are you using AI coding tools today?
You: I use them to analyse issues, compare solution options, and understand unfamiliar code.
Manager: Do you accept the first answer?
You: No. I add business and technical context, then validate the result with tests and project evidence.
Manager: What would improve the outcome?
You: Better project context, clear security rules, and agreed quality checks.

Cross-project alignment

Architect: Our project needs a custom framework.
You: What need is not covered by the common approach?
Architect: We need a different approval flow.
You: That sounds like a valid extension point. Let us keep the common core and isolate the approval rule.
Architect: Can you help us review the boundary?
You: Yes. I will compare it with the other projects and propose a reusable option.

Useful vocabulary and collocations

  • technical recommendation — đề xuất kỹ thuật có lý do
  • independent view — góc nhìn độc lập
  • cross-project risk — rủi ro ảnh hưởng nhiều dự án
  • production readiness — mức sẵn sàng production
  • thought partner — đối tác cùng phân tích và phản biện
MDtechnical-discussions.mdArchitecture review, incident evidence, test coverage · 38 lines⌄

Technical discussions

Thể hiện vai trò TA bằng việc làm rõ context, so sánh option, nêu risk và cách kiểm chứng.

Reusable phrases

Situation Natural sentence Simpler alternative More professional alternative
Ask for context Could you walk me through the current flow? How does it work now? Could you walk me through the current flow, including the main dependencies?
Challenge I see one risk with this approach. This may cause a problem. I have one concern about how this behaves during a partial failure.
Recommend I suggest we test this with one service first. Let us test it first. My recommendation is to run a small pilot and review the evidence before scaling it.
Validate What result would prove this works? How will we test it? Could we agree on the acceptance criteria and the evidence we need?

Realistic dialogue

Architecture review

Developer: We want every service to call the new API directly.
You: Could you show me the call flow and the failure path?
Developer: If the API is down, each service will retry.
You: That may create a retry storm. I suggest one retry policy, a clear timeout, and an idempotency check.
Architect: Can you review a small proof of concept?
You: Yes. Please include normal traffic, a timeout, and a 503 test. I will review the results tomorrow.

Incident evidence

Developer: The pod is running, so Kubernetes looks fine.
You: Running is one useful signal. Is the pod Ready, and is it processing work?
Developer: The queue is still growing.
You: Then the user impact is still present. Let us check worker logs, queue age, and the last deployment together.

Useful vocabulary and collocations

  • current flow — luồng hiện tại
  • failure path — luồng khi lỗi
  • acceptance criteria — tiêu chí chấp nhận
  • remaining risk — rủi ro còn lại
  • supporting evidence — bằng chứng hỗ trợ
